kitty_graphics.value: Broad, inside the crate. Transmission: t=d with chunking, t=f, t=t (path must contain tty-graphics-protocol; deleted after reading), t=s (shm_open on Unix, a file mapping on Windows). Formats: f=8, f=16, f=24, f=32 raw and f=100 PNG; PNG decodes only with the non-default `graphics` feature, otherwise EINVAL. o=z zlib with a decompressed-size cap. Placement: a=T and a=p at the cursor with x/y/w/h source rectangle, c/r cell span, X/Y sub-cell offset, C=1, z index. U=1 virtual placements are stored as metadata and ansi/kitty_virtual.rs supplies the placeholder decoders, but scanning cells for U+10EEEE and compositing is the embedder's renderer's job. Deletes: a/A, i/I, n/N, c/C, p/P, x/X, y/Y, z/Z, q/Q, r/R. a=q runs the real load path and answers OK or the error, honouring q=. Limits: 320 MiB image store per terminal with eviction of unreferenced images; 10000 px per axis and 400 MiB payload at parse; 4096x4096 display cap. Not implemented: animation (a=f, a=a, a=c answered EINVAL:unsupported action) and relative placements (P/Q/H/V parsed, never used).

kitty_tags.value: transmit-direct, transmit-file, transmit-temp, transmit-shm, format-png, format-raw, compression, place-direct, place-virtual, delete-by-id, delete-by-position, query-reply, z-layers
kitty_tags.note: [inferred] from the source read for kitty_graphics. Not tagged: animation (a=f/a/c rejected with EINVAL:unsupported action, kitty_graphics_protocol.rs:757-792). Caveats on tagged items: format-png only with the non-default `graphics` feature; place-virtual means the crate records U=1 placements and ships the decode helpers, while the per-frame U+10EEEE scan and drawing belong to the embedder (Rio's renderer and librio both do it); z-layers means the crate keeps z_index per placement and deletes by z, with drawing order left to the renderer (Rio's sorts by z at renderer/mod.rs:545). unknown: none

picture_anchoring.value: Absolute row counter in side tables, not per-cell: Kitty placements keep dest_row and Sixel/iTerm2 AtlasPlacements keep abs_row = lines_evicted + history + screen_row, so pictures scroll and survive scrollback eviction. On a column reflow a recorded ReflowRemap moves each placement to where its anchor row's content landed (Sixel/iTerm2 pieces on dropped rows are destroyed; Kitty ones stay). Text written over a Sixel/iTerm2 picture splits it into cropped children. Quota: total_limit 320 MiB per terminal, evicting images not in use.

grid_api.value: Crosswords<U: EventListener>, descended from alacritty's Term: visible_rows() -> Vec<Row<Square>>, fill_visible_rows(&mut Vec<Row<Square>>), snapshot_visible(damage, rows, row_styles, extras) for incremental copies with resolved styles, and pub grid: Grid<Square> indexed by Line and Column with display_iter(). A Square is a packed u64: c() base char, wide() Normal / Wide / Spacer / LeadingSpacer, cell_flags() WRAPLINE / HYPERLINK / GRAPHEME, plus style and extras ids. grid.style_of(&square) -> Style { fg, bg, underline_color: Option<AnsiColor>, flags: StyleFlags } (bold, dim, italic, inverse, hidden, strikeout, five underline kinds, blink). Zero-width marks: grid.cell_text(pos) yields the base char then the marks (Square::c() alone drops them); hyperlinks: cell_hyperlink(line, col). Cursor: cursor() -> CursorState; modes: mode() -> Mode, keyboard_mode().

damage_tracking.value: yes — per viewport line since the last reset: damage() returns TermDamage::Full or Partial(iterator of damaged lines) and reset_damage() clears it; snapshot_visible also marks each copied row dirty; a coarse TerminalDamage { Noop, Full, Partial, CursorOnly } signal travels in events
damage_tracking.note: quote: "/// Terminal damage information collected since the last [`Term::reset_damage`] call." — [measured] damage() at crosswords/mod.rs:592 and reset_damage() at :637; TerminalDamage at event/mod.rs:105-126. The 0.5.21 changelog entry describes a property test asserting that every changed row is covered by reported damage.

state_snapshot.value: Partial. Crosswords::contents_formatted() / format(FormatOptions::vt()) re-emits the visible screen as VT bytes: reset, clear, home, SGR runs with colours in their original named / indexed / RGB form, then cursor position and cursor visibility. It writes only each cell's base character, so combining marks are dropped, and carries no scrollback, hyperlinks, other modes, alt-screen state or pictures. librio's Surface::serialize() adds scrollback and OSC 8 links, but librio is publish = false. Crosswords implements neither Clone nor serde.

threading_and_loop.value: The embedder chooses. Headless, the embedder owns the loop and calls Processor::advance(&mut term, bytes) on a Crosswords it holds, with no threads. With the default `pty` feature, performer::Machine spawns a 'PTY reader' thread that polls a teletypewriter PTY through corcovado and parses into an Arc<FairMutex<Crosswords<U>>> shared with the renderer (U: EventListener + Send + 'static). Crosswords has no internal locking. The PTY layer (teletypewriter) is included and can be dropped with default-features = false. Synchronized updates: an embedder loop should poll Processor::sync_timeout(); otherwise advance() flushes an expired update when the next bytes arrive.
threading_and_loop.note:
quote: "Create a grid, feed it bytes through the parser, and read cells back. No
PTY, no renderer, no threads:" — [measured] Machine at rio-vt/src/performer/mod.rs:121-131, 203-215, 372-380; advance and the sync fallback at performer/handler.rs:598-621; no Rc, RefCell or Cell in the crate (grep), so Send follows the listener type.

reply_channel.value: An event callback. Replies (DA1/DA2, DSR/CPR, DECRQM, XTGETTCAP, Kitty acks and a=q answers) are sent as RioEvent::PtyWrite(route_id, String) through EventListener::send_event. Window-size reports arrive as TextAreaSizeRequest, OSC colour queries as ColorRequest and OSC 52 reads as ClipboardLoad, each carrying a formatter closure the embedder applies before writing. The embedder does the PTY write, so a TD replica can drop these events and let the host answer once — the same shape as alacritty's Event.

td_migration.value: A moderate rewrite, the smallest of the non-alacritty cores, because rio-vt's Crosswords, Grid, Storage, Row, selection, search and parser are forks of alacritty_terminal and vte (file headers cite alacritty e35e5ad) and its events mirror alacritty's (PtyWrite, TextAreaSizeRequest, ColorRequest, ClipboardLoad with formatter closures). term.rs: Term::new + Config become Crosswords::new(size, cursor shape, listener, WindowId, route_id, scrollback limit) with CrosswordsSize::new_with_dimensions, since Kitty spans need cell pixel sizes; TermEvent matching becomes RioEvent. host.rs and socketpty.rs: alacritty's EventLoop, Notifier, Msg and tty traits give way either to rio_vt::performer::Machine with a teletypewriter::EventedPty impl for SocketPty (corcovado polling instead of the polling crate) or to a TD-owned loop with default-features = false that calls Processor::advance and polls sync_timeout(); either way the attach fence must be re-proved. gridwire.rs: re-encode from Square + grid.style_of + cell_text + Wide + WRAPLINE instead of Cell and Flags, and hash resolved Style values rather than style ids, which are interned per grid and will differ between host and replica; pictures need their own channel because no snapshot carries them. pane.rs (51 grid reads): Cell fields become Square::c / wide plus Style plus Extras, Point / Side / Selection move to rio_vt types, TermMode becomes Mode; add a picture layer that drains UpdateGraphics, reads kitty_placements and atlas_placements, scans visible rows for U+10EEEE with the kitty_virtual helpers and paints in gpui. main.rs and pane/bench.rs: type renames. The window replica would decode pictures too unless the host forwards them.

kitty_graphics.value: Partial, and off unless the embedder turns it on (TerminalConfiguration::enable_kitty_graphics returns false by default). Transmission: t=d with chunking, t=f, t=t, t=s (POSIX shm through the kitty-shm feature, which termwiz's use_image enables). Formats f=24, f=32, f=100; o=z. a=t, a=T, a=p direct placements with source rectangle, c/r, X/Y offsets, C and z. a=q answers OK or ERROR. Animation frames a=f and composition a=c are handled; a=a playback control is not parsed. Deletes: only a/A and i/I; every other d= value (n/N, c, p, q, r, x, y, z) is logged as unhandled. No U=1 virtual placements or Unicode placeholders (no U key parsed, no U+10EEEE handling). Quota: 320 MiB hard-coded with a FIXME, pruning unreferenced image data. Same code on main b09b56c29c.

picture_anchoring.value: Per-cell attribute: every covered cell's CellAttributes holds a Vec<Box<ImageCell>> with that cell's texture-coordinate slice, an Arc<ImageData>, z_index, padding and the Kitty image and placement ids. Pictures therefore scroll into scrollback and are freed with their lines, and on reflow their slices wrap like text (inferred from the storage). Writing a cell drops its image slices unless they carry a Kitty placement id, so Sixel and iTerm2 pictures erase under text. Quota: 320 MiB for Kitty image data only (kitty.rs:47); other pictures live as long as their cells.

grid_api.value: Terminal derefs to TerminalState; screen() -> &Screen. Screen::lines_in_phys_range(range) -> Vec<Line>, visible_lines(), all_lines(), with_phys_lines(range, f), and conversions between physical, visible and stable row indices. Line::visible_cells() yields CellRef values (cell_index(), str() for the whole grapheme, width(), attrs()) and skips the blank cell a wide character covers. CellAttributes: foreground(), background(), underline_color(), intensity, underline kind, italic, reverse, strikethrough, invisible, overline, wrapped, hyperlink(), images(). Cursor: TerminalState::cursor_pos() -> CursorPosition. Modes through accessors such as is_alt_screen_active(), plus mouse and focus accessors added on main in September 2026 (#8045).

damage_tracking.value: yes — by sequence number: each Line records the seqno of its last change, TerminalState::current_seqno() gives the current one, and Screen::get_changed_stable_rows(range, seqno) returns the stable rows changed since a given seqno
damage_tracking.note:
quote: "pub fn get_changed_stable_rows(
        &self,
        stable_lines: Range<StableRowIndex>,
        seqno: SequenceNo,
    ) -> Vec<StableRowIndex> {" — [measured] Line::changed_since and current_seqno at wezterm-surface/src/line/line.rs:283-287; TerminalState::current_seqno at term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs:592. WezTerm's mux ships these as dirty_lines ranges (codec/src/lib.rs:919).

state_snapshot.value: No whole-terminal serializer and no VT re-encoder. With the use_serde feature, Line and Cell (with hyperlinks and image cells) are serde types, and WezTerm's own client/server mux sends SerializedLines (stable-row-indexed lines plus hyperlinks and images) with cursor, dimensions and dirty ranges: a line-level replica protocol rather than VT bytes. Modes, scroll regions, tab stops and parser state are not in that message (inferred from its fields).

threading_and_loop.value: The embedder owns the read loop and the PTY: feed bytes with Terminal::advance_bytes(bytes), or parse elsewhere and apply with perform_actions(Vec<Action>), which is what WezTerm's mux does from a reader thread. No PTY layer in the crate (WezTerm's is the separate portable-pty crate). Terminal::new spawns one writer thread per terminal (ThreadedWriter) that pushes replies into the supplied writer. WezTerm keeps each Terminal behind a Mutex; the configuration, clipboard and alert handler are Send + Sync trait objects.
threading_and_loop.note:
quote: "This crate does not provide any kind of gui, nor does it directly
manage a PTY; you provide a `std::io::Write` implementation that
could connect to a PTY, and supply bytes to the model via the
`advance_bytes` method." — [measured] advance_bytes and perform_actions at term/src/terminal.rs:159-185; ThreadedWriter spawns std::thread at term/src/terminalstate/mod.rs:446-478; Mutex<Terminal> at mux/src/localpane.rs:126; the Send + Sync bounds at terminal.rs:13 (Clipboard), :76 (AlertHandler) and config.rs:135 (TerminalConfiguration); pty/Cargo.toml:2 names portable-pty.

reply_channel.value: A Box<dyn std::io::Write + Send> passed to Terminal::new. DA1/DA2, DSR, DECRQM, window-size reports and Kitty a=q replies are written straight into it (through the per-terminal ThreadedWriter), as are keyboard and mouse encodings; title, bell, clipboard and palette changes go to an AlertHandler. There is no reply event to filter, so a TD replica would pass std::io::sink() and only the host's terminal would answer.

td_migration.value: The largest rewrite of the Rust candidates, since nothing maps one-to-one. host.rs and socketpty.rs: alacritty's EventLoop, Notifier and tty traits go with no replacement, so TD writes its own PTY read loop (which the Kitty work needs anyway), feeds Terminal::advance_bytes, and re-implements DEC 2026 synchronized output, which wezterm-term leaves to WezTerm's mux. term.rs: Term and Config become Terminal::new(TerminalSize, Arc<dyn TerminalConfiguration>, term_program, term_version, writer) with a TD TerminalConfiguration that switches on Kitty graphics and keyboard; the host passes the PTY writer, the replica std::io::sink(). gridwire.rs: rewrite the encoder over Screen, Line, CellRef and CellAttributes with stable row indices; pictures sit as ImageCell slices inside cell attributes, which a VT re-encode cannot carry, so either add a picture channel or replace gridwire with WezTerm-style serde SerializedLines. pane.rs (51 grid reads): Line::visible_cells and CellRef::str (grapheme strings instead of a char plus zero-width list), CellAttributes getters, per-cell image slices drawn in gpui with negative z under text; selection must be rebuilt because WezTerm keeps it in wezterm-gui (wezterm-gui/src/selection.rs), not in the crate. main.rs and pane/bench.rs: renames. Build: a git dependency on the wezterm workspace, which brings the finl_unicode git fork with it.

bubbles.note: Published rio-vt 0.5.28 depends on parking_lot ^0.12.5 with features nightly and hardware-lock-elision. Cargo unifies features, so adopting rio-vt would switch lock elision on for every parking_lot user in TD's graph, gpui included. On Linux x86 the nightly feature only affects wasm atomics in parking_lot_core 0.9.12 (lib.rs:48), so stable Rust still builds, but lock behaviour changes process-wide.
bubbles.why: a dependency swap that silently alters gpui's locking is worth a check before any spike

bubbles.note: rio-vt's README has drifted from its code: it says EventListener::event() is required (no such method in event/mod.rs:428-436), its feature table omits the default `pty` feature and the `graphics` feature that PNG and iTerm2 decoding need. An embedder following the README gets Kitty PNG answered with EINVAL.
bubbles.why: a spike should enable `graphics` explicitly and read the source, not the README

bubbles.note: Crosswords::contents_formatted() writes only each cell's base character (formatter.rs:128-129), so a replica restored from it loses combining marks; librio's Surface::serialize() (librio/src/lib.rs:896-960, MIT, built only on rio-vt's public API) handles scrollback and OSC 8 and is a portable reference if TD adopts rio-vt, though TD's gridwire.rs already does more.
bubbles.why: TD's host/replica hash comparison would flag the mark loss immediately

bubbles.note: The foundation review's 'maintainer absent' is out of date for commits: 147 of 182 commits since 2025-09-25 landed June to September 2026, Benoit de Chezelles (bew) is now the top committer, and a September 2026 commit (#8045) adds TerminalState accessors explicitly 'for downstream users'. It remains accurate for releases (none since 2024-02-03).
bubbles.why: the review's option F reasoning cites WezTerm as stalled; half of that premise has changed

bubbles.note: WezTerm's own mux is prior art for TD's host/replica split, done differently: the server keeps the only emulator and clients receive serde SerializedLines plus dirty stable-row ranges keyed by sequence number (codec GetPaneRenderChangesResponse), with images shipped as SerializedImageCell, instead of re-encoded VT bytes and a hash check.
bubbles.why: a line-level wire protocol would carry pictures to the window, which TD's VT snapshot cannot
